short: Phone-model decoder (M06) is the EMG recognizer moved to ECoG: standard. 25% WER uses per-phrase dictionaries holding the spoken words (M07); the time-shift null (M12) is sound.
position: Brain-to-Text [@herff2015] changes the decoder (M06): Gaussian phone models on ECoG broadband gamma, joined to a dictionary and a bigram model by Viterbi search. This is standard: it is the continuous EMG recognizer of the same group [@jou2006; @schultz2010] on a new signal, so the Abstract's priority claim concerns ECoG, not decoding. The lexicon (M07) is the weak point: each test phrase gets a dictionary containing its spoken words (§2.11), and bigrams come from the read texts with no stated exclusion of the test phrase (§2.10), whereas the EMG prior kept test sentences out of its language model [@jou2006]. The 25% WER is a closed-set figure, not comparable with the 25% median WER of [later] ECoG work on a 1,024-word set [@metzger2023]. The evaluation (M12) is standard; its time-shifted null, keeping dictionary and language model, is the strongest design choice. Scaling to vocabularies without the spoken words, and generalisation beyond the session, remain unsupported.
